title: The Fire on the Hill
synopsis: Spring 1919: students in Seoul are calling for independence.
Near Cheonan, Yu Gwan-sun plans a march at Aunae Market.
But a wrong day is going round the villages.
goal: Find the true day of the march, and the sign that tells the villages.

options.label: The second of April
options.feedback: Only Mr. Pyo says the second. Find two people who say the same day.

options.label: The tenth of March
options.feedback: Nobody says March. Ask each person about the day again.

notes: Played as a talk (DialogueScene) at the market: Gyeongsun and Dong-il both carried the first of April; Mr. Pyo, a made-up salt seller, says the second.
Then: Mr. Pyo says a stranger paid him to ask (pyo.who): paid off in the final, where the plan is locked away with the true days.
The background is the market's place picture; the three witnesses are their base portraits.

learning.objective: 세 사람에게 같은 질문(What day did you tell the villages?)을 하고, 같은 날을 말한 두 사람의 진술을 찾는다.
expressions: What day did you tell the villages?
Two of them say the same day.

play.title: Three Messengers
story: Aunae Market is busy with baskets, rice and salt.
Under your teacup at the noodle stall, a folded note waits.
It is written in Hangeul. In the corner is a small water drop.
play.letter:
Three people told Gwan-sun's day to the villages.
Two of them say the same day.
One man says another day. Someone paid him to ask.
Ask what each one heard.
— a small water drop
play.question: What is the true day of the march?
hints: Ask every person the same question about the day.
Two people say the same thing. Compare their answers.
play.successMessage: Two messengers say the same day!
transition: The march is on the first of April, the big market day.
But how will far villages know the time has come?
Gyeongsun takes your arm. "Come to Gwan-sun's house."

clue.note: Two messengers say the march is on the first of April.

witnesses.greeting: I carried the day to two villages.

day.line: The big market day. The first of April.

witnesses.greeting: I ran to five villages. I am fast!

day.line: The second of April. I am sure of it.

place.line: At the train station, I think.

discovery.title: THE FIRST OF APRIL
discovery.detail: Two messengers agree. But a stranger is asking questions too.

options.label: A fire burns on Maebong hill

notes: Gwan-sun's plan, read out of order with when, before, the night before and in the morning. The bell is a decoy her plan rules out (too loud).
Her words are made up (dossier fiction); the sign itself, a fire on Maebong hill the night before the march, is history (h3).

clueInputs.note: The march is on the first of April, market day.

learning.objective: when, before, the night before, in the morning을 읽고 계획의 네 단계를 순서대로 놓는다.
expressions: When the market is full, we start the march.

play.title: Gwan-sun's Plan
story: Yu Gwan-sun studies at Ewha School in Seoul. It is closed now.
She came home with one big idea.
"The police watch the roads," she says. "We cannot send letters."
play.letterIntro: Gwan-sun's plan, written in a hurry:
play.letter:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people walk to the market, like shoppers.
They come because they saw our sign the night before.
Our sign is a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell. A bell is too loud.
play.question: Put the plan in order, from the first step to the last.
hints: Find the step that happens the night before.
The morning comes after the night. The march starts last.
transition: Fire, then the walk, then a full market, then the march.
Every village can see Maebong hill at night.
Gwan-sun smiles. "No letter can be stolen. A fire is the letter."
play.orderFeedback: Those are the right steps. Read when each one happens again.

clue.note: The night before the march, a fire on the hill tells the villages.

evidence.name: Gwan-sun's Plan
evidence.description: The sign is a fire on Maebong hill, the night before the market day.
evidence.inscription: Our sign is a fire on Maebong hill.

talk.speaker: yu_gwansun
talk.goal: Find out how the villages will know.

lines.text: People in Seoul called for independence. Now it is our turn.
But how will far villages know the time?
I wrote my plan. But I wrote it all mixed up.

discovery.title: A LETTER MADE OF FIRE
discovery.detail: The villages will know by the fire. But the stranger is still asking.

notes: Three made-up girls' notebooks, told apart by the words: only one is in Hangeul with a water drop by the name. Mrs. Kang's note of 1909 (s5_ep07_e1, recalled) carries the same mark.
Gwan-sun's school friends here are made up; Gwan-sun's words are made up.

clueInputs.note: Mrs. Kang's water-drop note of 1909: the same small water drop.

expressions: A small water drop sits by her name.

play.title: Three Notebooks
story: Three school friends of Gwan-sun's are home from Seoul too.
Their notebooks lie on the low table.
Who wrote the note with the water drop?
play.letterIntro: What you see on the table:
play.letter:
Sunja's notebook: a pressed flower on the cover. She writes in Chinese characters.
Okhui's notebook: a blue ribbon. She draws little stars by her name.
Gyeongsun's notebook: plain and brown. On its label, a small water drop sits by her name.
Your note: written on thin paper, only in Hangeul, with a small water drop.
play.question: Who wrote the water-drop note? Type her name.
hints: Look at your note first: what mark does it have?
Which notebook has the same mark by the name?
transition: "My family has used that water drop for a long time."
"Tonight, on the hill, I will show you why."

feedback.SUNJA: Sunja writes in Chinese characters. Your note is only in Hangeul.
feedback.OKHUI: Okhui draws stars, not water drops. Look at the notebooks again.
feedback.GWANSUN: Gwan-sun's notebook is not on the table. Read the three notebooks.

lines.text: Mrs. Kang in Harbin is my family too.
Her note has the very same water drop.
We all learned it from the same old box.

discovery.title: ONE MARK, ONE FAMILY
discovery.detail: Harbin in 1909, Aunae in 1919: the same water drop. What is in the old box?

notes: The keepers' letter box, locked by Gyeongsun with the plan's two days: the night of the sign (the last night of March, 31) and the day of the march (the first of April, 1). Both days are history (h2, h3); the lock and the box are made up.
Mr. Pyo's day (the second of April) would make 012: the stranger cannot open it.

clueInputs.note: First two dials: the night before the march, the last night of March (31).
Last dial: the first of April (1).
Bun-i's note of 1446 lies at the bottom of the box (shown in the ending).

learning.objective: the night before, March has thirty-one days를 읽고 신호의 날(31)과 행진의 날(1)을 다이얼로 맞춘다.

play.title: The Fire on the Hill
story: At dusk, Gyeongsun leads you up Maebong hill.
She carries an old wooden box with a small dial lock.
"I put Gwan-sun's plan inside. The stranger must not read it."
play.letter:
I set the lock to our two days.
First two dials: the night of the sign. It is a night in March.
Last dial: the day of the march, in April.
Remember: March has thirty-one days.
The sign burns the night before the march.
play.question: Turn the dials to the night of the sign and the day of the march.
hints: Your notes say the day of the march. Your plan says when the sign burns.
The night before the first of April is the last night of March.
transition: Below, the villages are dark and quiet.
Then a small flame rises on Maebong hill.
Far away, on other hills, you see more lights.

feedback.131: First the night of the sign, then the day of the march.
feedback.301: March has thirty-one days. The night before April 1 is the last night of March.
feedback.302: The march is on the first of April, not the second.
feedback.012: That is Mr. Pyo's day. Two messengers said the first of April.

play.orderFeedback: These numbers fit, but not in this order. The night of the sign comes first.

evidence.name: The Keepers' Letter Box
evidence.description: An old wooden letter box. Gwan-sun's plan is on top. Bun-i's note of 1446 is at the bottom.
evidence.inscription: The night of the sign, then the day of the march.

ending.text: Under the plan lie old notes, each with a water drop.
The oldest is at the bottom. One corner is burnt.
ending.speaker: gyeongsun

ending.text: It says 훈민정음. This is Bun-i's note from 1446!
Bun-i was our first keeper. We are all her family.
ending.speaker: gyeongsun

ending.text: That night, Gwan-sun lights the fire on Maebong hill.
On 1 April 1919, thousands of people gather at Aunae Market.
Gwan-sun leads them. They call for Korea's independence.

hook: The keepers are one family. Where will the box go next?

objectives: Find the true day of the march.
Read the plan for the sign.
Find who wrote the water-drop note.
intro: Spring, 1919. You are a guest of Yu Gwan-sun's family, near Cheonan.
In March, students in Seoul called for independence.
The schools were closed, so Gwan-sun came home.
Now she and the village elders plan a march at Aunae Market.
But the police watch the roads, and a wrong day is going round.
play.caseSummary: Two messengers said the true day: the first of April. Gwan-sun's sign was a fire on Maebong hill the night before. Gyeongsun, a keeper, showed the old box with Bun-i's note at the bottom. On 1 April 1919, Gwan-sun led thousands of people at Aunae Market. They called for Korea's independence.

notes: PART 10 Case 08 (Act 2's reveal): the keepers are one family; the box ends here as s5_ep08_e4 and goes to Shanghai with Haesu (Case 09).

Yu Gwan-sun is real, her words are made up (dossier fiction). Gyeongsun, Dong-il, Mr. Pyo, the stranger, the notebooks and the box are made up. The case ends on history: the sign the night before and the march of 1 April 1919 (h2, h3); her arrest and death in 1920 are told once, in the reveal.
